Everything between the tags is untrusted data from GitHub. { "number": 35901, "title": "wallet: Fix ScanForWalletTransactions missing tx when look-ahead pool expands mid-block", "author": "pablomartin4btc", "author_association": "MEMBER", "created": "2026-08-05", "draft": false, "participants": [ "jeanpablojp (contributor, 3 statements, 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-29)", "achow101 (member, 2 statements, 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-10)", "molnard (none, 4 statements, 2026-08-27 to 2026-08-27)", "vicjuma (contributor, 2 statements, 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-06)", "polespinasa (member, 1 statement, 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-06)", "w0xlt (contributor, 2 statements, 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-07)" ] } When `ScanForWalletTransactions` processes a block containing both a transaction to a key just outside the look-ahead pool and a pool-expanding transaction that triggers `TopUp`, and the former appears first in vtx order, the wallet misses the earlier transaction — leaving the balance wrong with no indication a second scan is needed. The fix retries any transaction that doesn't match on a full pass, dropping it once it does, until a pass resolves nothing new — so a transaction can be recognized once something else in the block makes it relevant, regardless of why. The first commit demonstrates the incorrect behaviour; the second contains the fix; the third adds a benchmark guarding the fix's performance on a large, mostly-foreign block with an embedded multi-level cascade. Bug details... `ScanForWalletTransactions` iterates over a block's transactions in the order the miner placed them (vtx order). A descriptor wallet maintains a look-ahead pool of pre-derived keys so it can recognise incoming payments. When a payment arrives at a key near the pool boundary, `MarkUnusedAddresses` → `TopUp` extends the pool. If within a single block: - **Tx_lookahead** pays to key index `N` (just outside the current pool `[0, N-1]`), AND - **Tx_expand** pays to key index `N-1` (last in pool — triggers TopUp, extending pool to `[0, 2N-1]`) and Tx_lookahead appears at an earlier vtx position than Tx_expand, the scan misses Tx_lookahead: 1. Tx_lookahead processed: pool = `[0, N-1]` → `IsMine` returns false → missed 2. Tx_expand processed: key `N-1` found → TopUp fires → pool = `[0, 2N-1]` `FastWalletRescanFilter::UpdateIfNeeded()` fires only at the **start of the next block** iteration — there is no mechanism to re-examine Tx_lookahead within the same scan pass. The transaction is not permanently lost — because Tx_expand extended the pool as a side effect, a second explicit `rescanblockchain` call recovers Tx_lookahead. But the wallet shows a wrong balance with no indication a second scan is needed. This bug does not affect live `blockConnected` when both transactions pass through the mempool first: `transactionAddedToMempool(Tx_expand)` pre-extends the pool before the block arrives, so vtx ordering does not matter. It only manifests in `ScanForWalletTransactions` (rescan paths) for descriptor wallets. Affected callers... **Callers affected** (all use `ScanForWalletTransactions`): - `rescanblockchain` - `importdescriptors` (via `RescanFromTime`) - `restorewallet` and wallet migration watchonly/solvable wallets (via `AttachChain`) Fix details and performance... **Fix:** during the per-block vtx loop, keep a list of still-unmatched vtx positions. Retry it each pass, dropping positions once `SyncTransaction()` returns `true` for them, until a full pass resolves nothing new. A transaction becomes resolvable once something else earlier in the same block changes its relevance — either a pool expansion (`TopUp` from `MarkUnusedAddresses`) now covering a key it pays, or a previously-unknown parent transaction becoming known so a spend of it is recognized. The unmatched set never grows, so this terminates without a safety cap. This also covers two cases a shrinking-prefix rescan (an earlier version of this fix) did not: a prefix-recovered receive that triggers a second pool expansion past where the prefix had already shrunk to (see Part 5), and a same-block spend of a look-ahead receive only recognized later in the same pass via a parent-tx lookup rather than a pool expansion (see Part 6, molnard's finding — see Notes below). **Performance:** the retry loop costs at most one extra pass for any block containing a wallet-relevant transaction during a rescan, in typical shapes. The worst case is a large, mostly-foreign block with a multi-level cascade embedded in it. `bench_bitcoin -filter=RescanCascadeInLargeBlock` guards that scenario against regression. Test coverage... **Regression test:** `test/functional/wallet_rescan_intrablock_ordering.py` - Part 1: loadwallet rescan — Tx_lookahead found after fix. - Part 2: importdescriptors full rescan from genesis — Tx_lookahead found after fix. - Part 3: second rescanblockchain recovers Tx_lookahead (pre-fix behaviour, kept as sanity check). - Part 4: two-level cascade — two successive TopUp events fire in one block, both lookahead txs found, validating the bounded multi-pass loop. - Part 5: a prefix-recovered receive triggers a second TopUp past where a shrinking-prefix rescan would have already stopped. - Part 6: a same-block spend of a look-ahead receive only recognized later in the same pass (molnard's finding). Manual reproduction (regtest) ```bash bitcoind -regtest -keypool=5 -fallbackfee=0.0001 -daemon bitcoin-cli -regtest -named createwallet wallet_name=funding bitcoin-cli -regtest generatetoaddress 102 $(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=funding getnewaddress) bitcoin-cli -regtest -named createwallet wallet_name=test RECV_DESC=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listdescriptors \ | jq -r '[.descriptors[] | select(.internal==false and .range!=null)][0].desc') END_RANGE=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listdescriptors \ | jq '[.descriptors[] | select(.internal==false and .range!=null)][0].range[1]') ADDR_EXPAND=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest deriveaddresses "$RECV_DESC" "[$END_RANGE,$END_RANGE]" | jq -r '.[0]') ADDR_LOOKAHEAD=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest deriveaddresses "$RECV_DESC" "[$((END_RANGE+1)),$((END_RANGE+1))]" | jq -r '.[0]') bitcoin-cli -regtest unloadwallet test TXID1=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=funding sendtoaddress "$ADDR_LOOKAHEAD" 0.001) TXID2=$(bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=funding sendtoaddress "$ADDR_EXPAND" 0.001) bitcoin-cli -regtest generateblock "raw(51)" "[\"$TXID1\",\"$TXID2\"]" # First scan — TXID1 missing, wrong balance bitcoin-cli -regtest loadwallet test bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listtransactions # Second scan — TXID1 recovered bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test rescanblockchain bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listtransactions # With the fix (this PR's tip), both transactions are found on the first scan. bitcoin-cli -regtest loadwallet test bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcwallet=test listtransactions ``` _**Notes**_: * Originally noted by furszy in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31629#issuecomment-2657775368; his "case 2" describes a related but harder inter-block variant: new blocks arriving via `blockConnected` during an active rescan with a not-yet-expanded pool. That problem remains a potential follow-up. This PR fixes the simpler intra-block sub-case where the miss happens entirely within a single block's vtx loop, with no concurrent block arrivals required. * Perhaps the issue is related to the symptom was previously reported in #19808 but could not be reproduced at the time and was closed without a fix. * molnard [found](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35901#pullrequestreview-5041935034) a related gap the shrinking-prefix rescan didn't close: if a parent tx pays a look-ahead key and a later tx in the same block spends that parent's output, and the spend sits at or after the block's last pool expansion, the prefix rescan recovers the parent but never revisits the spend. jeanpablojp separately found a second gap in the same shrinking-prefix approach — a prefix-recovered receive that triggers a further pool expansion past where the prefix had already shrunk to (Part 5) — and proposed and benchmarked the fix now in this PR: retry based on each tx's `SyncTransaction()` result until a full pass causes no change, rather than tracking a shrinking prefix. The PR description needs updating — the current approach goes through the entire block, not a prefix. **On "1, 2, 3 blocks before" / "why not N previous blocks"**: real gap, not fixed by this PR — the retry loop is strictly intra-block, so a block already scanned is never revisited even if a later block's TopUp expands it. No concurrency needed, so it's distinct from the @furszy case already in the description. A fixed N doesn't really solve it either — any N can be beaten by a long enough confirmation delay, and blindly rescanning N whole blocks is expensive (full re-fetch/reprocess, not just what's relevant). I'm looking at tracking unresolved candidates directly instead — by descriptor index for receives, by txid-dependency for spends. I think it's worth its own, orthogonal follow-up, which I'm planning to open soon. **On the performance-loss metric**: I don't think is needed here — the retry loop is bounded by construction (at most one extra pass, bounded by the block's own size), not a tunable tradeoff. **On how slow this gets**: each block's retry is independent, so earlier TopUp events don't compound later cost. Worst case benchmarked — a large, mostly-foreign block with a three-level cascade (`bench_bitcoin -filter=RescanCascadeInLargeBlock`) — ~80ms for the real `Scan()` call. Typical blocks cost one extra pass, converging immediately. Repeated TopUp mid-scan also isn't the common case — live `getnewaddress` already tops up ahead of use, so this mainly matters for restores/imports/migrations catching up to real history.
